extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers seeking to develop clear, strong themes in short stories or novels (novice to intermediate)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for identifying, developing, and testing a story's theme and writing a clear thematic statement that expresses the story's argument. Applies to fiction writers shaping character arcs, plot events, motifs, and revision to embody theme rather than announce it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-word subject the story explores (love, hate, greed, fear, freedom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the core subject area as a concise noun to focus the thematic work; this is the raw materia from which a thematic statement is formed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thematic statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete sentence stating the story's argument about the topic ("Greed isolates those who pursue it.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the theme as an assertive sentence (not a word). Treat it as the answer to the story's central question; it should be debatable and specific rather than a vague platitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premise (Egri)
rubrics_metrics.description: The same idea as a thematic statement, framed as a debatable proposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use premise wording when you want a compact, arguable formulation of what the story contends; useful for plotting and testing conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme should be implied, not stated
rubrics_metrics.description: Theme lives implicitly in the story rather than being directly told to the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid authorial exposition of the theme; let readers infer the argument from events, choices, and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme embodied in character arcs
rubrics_metrics.description: The characters' internal changes and arcs should incarnate the theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make protagonist growth or decline illustrate the thematic claim; what the protagonist learns (or refuses to learn) points to the theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme tested through plot events
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot events should repeatedly test the thematic question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design scenes that pose the thematic dilemma in different ways, so the story explores the ramifications of the thematic claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme reinforced through symbol and motif
rubrics_metrics.description: Recurring imagery and motifs support and point to the theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use symbols, recurring objects, or images to echo and deepen the thematic thread without spelling it out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start with a question (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with a question like "What does it cost to forgive?" — the story dramatizes the question and the theme is the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate a central question to dramatize; use it to shape plot choices and scenes so the story explores possible answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mine character arcs (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Look at what the protagonist learns; the lesson they learn is likely the theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the protagonist's change as a diagnostic: articulate what they learn and consider turning that into a thematic statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look at the antagonist's argument (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: The antagonist often embodies the counter-thesis to the theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast the protagonist's emerging belief with the antagonist's position to dramatize the thematic conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify recurring imagery (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recurring motifs point to theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalog images and motifs that keep reappearing in draft; they often reveal the story's real thematic concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find what you're scared to say (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your real theme is often something you almost don't want to acknowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be honest and brave in identifying uncomfortable or risky thematic statements — they can be more powerful and true than safe platitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discover during drafting (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many writers find theme only in revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow theme to emerge through writing and revising; use subsequent drafts to refine and align events, arcs, and motifs with the discovered theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can you state the thematic argument in one sentence? (test)
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong theme can be summarized as a single-sentence argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot produce a clear one-sentence thematic statement, the story's thematic focus may be fuzzy and needs tightening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does every major scene engage the theme? (test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each major scene should relate to the thematic question in some way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit scenes: if a scene never touches the theme, consider revising, removing, or repurposing it to serve thematic development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the climax dramatize the thematic question? (test)
rubrics_metrics.description: The climax should address the central thematic dilemma head-on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the climax forces the protagonist to make the thematic choice or face the thematic consequence; the thematic stakes should be highest here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the ending resolve (or refuse to resolve) the theme? (test)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ending should provide a resolution or deliberate refusal to resolve the thematic question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether your ending affirms, negates, complicates, or withholds the thematic answer and make that choice clear through consequences, not exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the theme embodied rather than announced? (test)
rubrics_metrics.description: The theme should be shown through action and change, not told through statements or speeches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid scenes that exist only to state the theme; prefer scenes that reveal it through character decisions and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid authorial notes / direct statement of theme (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not insert authorial explanation or explicit statements of the theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist narration or asides that tell the reader the theme; these break immersion and reduce subtlety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid characters delivering speeches that state the theme (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't rely on characters to lecture the theme to the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long expository speeches that declare the theme feel unrealistic and undermine dramatic tension; show through action instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid theme as a moral lesson lectured at reader (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theme should not become a moralizing lesson shoved at the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust readers to derive meaning; avoid didactic endings or contrived moral conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid theme that doesn't match the actual story events (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theme must be consistent with what actually happens in the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your declared theme contradicts character choices or plot outcomes, revise either the events or the thematic claim so they align.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid multiple competing themes that fight for attention (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Too many conflicting themes dilute focus and weaken the story's argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize and streamline thematic threads; if multiple themes exist, make one primary and let others support or complicate it without conflicting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague themes that mean nothing (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Steer clear of bland generalities like "love is good."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make thematic claims specific, debatable, and grounded in the story's events rather than platitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major universal theme categories
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-exhaustive list of common theme topics: Identity / self-discovery; Love and loss; Coming of age; Power and corruption; Justice and revenge; Freedom vs. duty; Tradition vs. change; Mortality; Faith and doubt; Nature vs. civilization; The individual vs. society; Truth and deception; Family bonds and conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list as a starting point to name your theme topic; pick a category and then craft a specific, arguable thematic statement about it.
